title: Product HUD loop and camera story
summary: A dense sci-fi HUD canvas showing how a product's system works, as a seamless music loop, then camera-flight stories across it with captions, localised versions, a brand logo intro and HQ plus social deliveries.

notFor.when: the film shows the product's real screens, app or website, or how to use them
a conventional product launch or ad that sells with real UI, product shots and a call to action
an existing still infographic, diagram or poster should move as a loop
an ident, kinetic type or abstract piece with no product system to depict
a voice-over film that teaches how something works step by step
only translating or dubbing an existing finished video

qa: Every element on the canvas stands for a real process of the product; every connector ends on a visible node, never in empty space
Loop: frame N renders identical to frame 0 (seam composition, cmp or difference YMAX 0); an approved render stays byte-identical after later edits
Story: first and last frames are black (Y max 16), every caption is readable at playback size before it leaves, every flight lands on a downbeat
Localised version: no overflow in any box, no translated code identifiers, numbers in the language's own format
Logo intro: the mark's last intro frame matches the canvas mark's size and position by bounding box; the soundtrack is unchanged
Master true peak at or below -0.5 dBFS and no FLASH_RISK from flash:check

intake.ask: Which product, and which of its real processes should the canvas show (import, indexing, search, agents, privacy)? Is there a design system or palette to use?
intake.why: Every block visualises a real process; the product's own palette and type override any starter style

intake.ask: Which track, and is it licensed for this use?
intake.why: The loop length and every arrival sit on its beat map; agents cannot hear, the user chooses by ear

intake.ask: Which deliverables: loops only, or also camera stories; which languages; HQ and which social sizes?
intake.why: Story, localisation and intro each add a round of approval; the order is loop, story EN, other languages, intro
intake.default: 30 s loops at 4:5, HQ x2 and 1080x1350 social; stories and languages offered after the loops are approved

intake.ask: Is there a brand logo animation (app launch, splash) to open the stories, and may its frames be used in the film?
intake.why: A third-party engine's licence may allow use in the end product but not redistributing its source
intake.default: No intro: the canvas mark builds on its own

intake.ask: Which names, logos and partner brands may appear publicly?
intake.why: Integration partners and data sources often cannot be named in public material yet
intake.default: Fictional people and data; partner names only with the user's yes

profiles.note: Delivered at 4:5, 1080x1350 (closest enum value is vertical). Captions are designed plates in the picture, not speech subtitles. Bands are house rules from one project.
HQ master at 2160x2700 (4:5, rendered at scale 2); loops end on their first frame, stories start and end on black so they loop too. House rule.

starter.note: A dark, precise Geist look fits a HUD; the product's own palette and type tokens override it. The blocks are a starting point: a dense canvas usually needs a project kit of panels, sparks, meters and comets built on them

variants.title: Seamless HUD loop
variants.changes: One canvas, length a whole number of bars (30 s at 160 BPM = 20 bars); all motion periodic in the loop length; a seam composition of N+1 frames proves frame N equals frame 0

variants.title: Camera-flight story over the canvas
variants.changes: Builds on an approved loop: a storyboard table first, then a shot table with arrivals on downbeats, build windows, caption pairs and SFX cues per flight; opens from black, ends on a pull-back to the whole canvas and black

evidence.project: Three 30 s HUD loops of a personal-memory product's system, then six 48 s camera stories (three canvases, EN and RU) with a captured app launch intro, HQ and 1080x1350 social
